## Natural history notes

A small heat-tolerant ant characterized by its tiny brown to yellowish-brown workers, fast movements, and habit of foraging during hot sunny periods when many other ants are less active. In Florida, the High Noon Ant is found in open sandy habitats such as scrub, sandhills, pine flatwoods, roadsides, lawns, fields, and disturbed ground where it nests in soil with small, low-profile entrances. Workers forage for dead insects, tiny arthropods, nectar, seeds, and honeydew, often moving quickly across bare ground and helping recycle small food resources in hot, open habitats.
